Change c0499. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. VII; 1831 Ch. XXIV.

Context before (unchanged): If I do, swear to me, Walton, that he shall not escape; that you will seek him, and satisfy my vengeance in his death.

1818 text: Yet, do I dare ask you to undertake my pilgrimage, to endure the hardships that I have undergone?

1831 text: And do I dare to ask of you to undertake my pilgrimage, to endure the hardships that I have undergone?

Diff: [-Yet,-] {+And+} do I dare {+to+} ask {+of+} you to undertake my pilgrimage, to endure the hardships that I have undergone?

Context after (unchanged): No; I am not so selfish.

result.rationale: Replaces 'Yet,' with 'And' and adds 'to' and 'of' ('do I dare to ask of you'); the request's meaning is unchanged, only its syntax and connective shift, a stylistic adjustment in Victor's diction.
